title: Chapter 2 – The Chemical Level of Organization
notes: Matter has mass and occupies space; chemistry studies its structure and interactions.
Major biological elements: O, C, H, N (plus Ca, P, K, S, Na, Cl, Mg).
Atomic number equals protons; mass number equals protons + neutrons.
Isotopes vary in neutrons; some are radioactive with characteristic half‑lives.
Ions: cations (+) lose electrons; anions (−) gain electrons.
Covalent bonds share electrons; ionic bonds transfer; hydrogen bonds are weak attractions.
Polarity depends on electronegativity differences—polar vs nonpolar covalent bonds.
Reaction types: synthesis, decomposition, exchange, reversible, redox.
Catalysts lower activation energy; enzymes are biological catalysts.
Energy forms: potential, kinetic, chemical; energy is conserved.
Water’s polarity underlies solvent properties, cohesion, high heat capacity and vaporization.
Mixtures: solutions, colloids, suspensions—differ by particle size/behavior.
Acids donate H+, bases donate OH− (or accept H+); salts dissociate into ions.
pH = −log[H+]; buffers resist pH changes (bicarbonate system).
Organic molecules: carbon skeletons with functional groups determine behavior.
Carbohydrates: mono-, di-, polysaccharides; glycogen is major storage polysaccharide.
Lipids: triglycerides, phospholipids, steroids; amphipathic phospholipids form bilayers.
Proteins: amino acids, peptide bonds, structure levels (primary→quaternary).
Denaturation disrupts protein structure & function (temperature, pH).
Enzyme activity depends on temperature, pH, and substrate concentration.
Nucleic acids store/express genetic information.
ATP is the immediate energy currency; regenerated by catabolic pathways.
Hydrogen bonds stabilize macromolecules and give water cohesion.
Dehydration synthesis builds polymers; hydrolysis breaks them.
Free radicals have unpaired electrons; antioxidants can neutralize them.

flashcards.back: Ions have net charge; atoms are neutral.
Stabilizes proteins/DNA; key to water properties.
Resist pH changes by binding/releasing H+.
Hydrophilic head + two hydrophobic tails; amphipathic.
Loss of protein structure/function due to environmental changes.
Immediate energy currency for cellular work.
Builds polymers (remove water) vs breaks polymers (add water).

flashcards.front: Why is water a good solvent?
flashcards.back: Polarity hydrates ions and polar molecules.

quiz.question: Water’s high heat capacity due to:
A buffer:
options: Converts strong acids/bases to weak ones
quiz.explanation: Binds/releases H+ to resist pH change.
